title: Workflow engine types: Workflow trait, StepResult, WaitCondition, WorkflowContext
description:
# Task: Workflow engine types

## Goal
Define the type system for durable workflows.

## Deliverables
- `Workflow` trait:
  - name/description
  - `handles(detection)` selector
  - `steps()` list
  - `execute_step(ctx, step_idx) -> StepResult`
  - optional `cleanup()`
- `WorkflowContext`:
  - references to WezTerm client + StorageHandle
  - pane_id + current `PaneCapabilities` snapshot
  - triggering event/detection
  - workflow config
- `StepResult`:
  - Continue
  - Done(result)
  - Retry(after)
  - Abort(reason)
  - WaitFor(condition, timeout)
- `WaitCondition`:
  - Pattern { pane_id, pattern }
  - PaneIdle { pane_id }
  - External { key }

## Why
We want workflows that are explicit state machines with a uniform execution model, so we can:
- persist/resume reliably
- test step logic deterministically
- share a single runner across agent-specific workflows

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - a stub workflow compiles and can be executed by a test runner
  - `StepResult` transitions are exhaustive (no “unknown” states)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Types compile and are used by a stub workflow + stub runner in tests.
- The type set is sufficient to express: send, wait, retry, abort, and done semantics.

title: Event handling semantics: dedupe, handled/unhandled transitions, idempotency, cooldowns
description:
# Task: Event handling semantics (idempotency + UX)

## Goal
Make the event→workflow loop reliable and user-friendly:
- events don’t spam
- events don’t get lost
- users can see what is unhandled and why
- workflows are idempotent across restarts

## Concepts
### Event states
Minimum required lifecycle states:
- `unhandled`
- `in_progress` (optional; set when workflow starts)
- `handled_completed`
- `handled_aborted`
- `handled_failed`

User-facing safety/UX requires one more explicit concept:
- `handled_paused` (or `handled_aborted` with a `paused_needs_human` reason)

**Paused meaning:** automation intentionally stopped because continuing would be unsafe or impossible without human action (MFA required, missing prerequisite, ambiguous pane state). Paused events must:
- not show up in `--unhandled` (to avoid “spam/retry loops”)
- remain visible in the events feed with a clear status + “next steps” payload

### Next-step plans (for paused)
When pausing, workflows should persist a structured, redacted “next step plan” so humans/agents can recover without guessing:
- what happened (high-level, redacted)
- what action is required (e.g., “complete MFA in browser profile X”)
- when to retry (e.g., reset time)
- any relevant identifiers (resume id, external id) in redacted/hashed form

Store this in workflow step logs and/or event metadata, and surface via:
- `wa robot events`
- `wa events` (human)

### Idempotency
Workflows should be able to re-run safely:
- if an event is already handled/paused, workflow runner should normally skip
- `--force` can override skip, but still policy-gated
- after restart, runner must not “forget” handled/paused state

### Dedupe/cooldowns
For noisy patterns, we need suppression:
- `dedupe_key` stored on events
- cooldown window per `(pane_id, rule_id)`
- if within cooldown:
  - either don’t insert new event, or insert but mark as suppressed

## Deliverables
- Clear rules for when the watcher inserts events vs suppresses.
- Runner behavior for:
  - selecting next unhandled event
  - marking `in_progress`
  - marking handled with execution status
  - marking paused with an explicit next-step plan payload
- CLI/robot-visible semantics:
  - `wa events --unhandled` is stable
  - handled/paused events record which workflow handled them

## Testing
- Unit tests for dedupe + cooldown decisions.
- Integration tests that simulate repeated detections and confirm:
  - no event spam
  - correct handled/paused status transitions
  - paused events are visible but not “re-executed” automatically
  - restart/resume: persisted state prevents re-running handled events after restart

## Acceptance Criteria
- Repeated identical detections do not create an unbounded event backlog.
- After a workflow completes, the corresponding event no longer appears in `--unhandled`.
- When automation pauses, the event is clearly marked and includes a redacted next-step plan.
close_reason: done

title: Workflow audit integration: record per-step actions/outcomes into audit trail
description:
# Task: Workflow audit integration

## Goal
Ensure workflows are explainable and trustworthy by recording an audit trail for every workflow action attempt.

Workflows can:
- send text
- issue control sequences (Ctrl-C)
- wait for conditions
- perform account/device-auth steps (later)

Users need to know exactly what wa did and why.

## Requirements
- For each workflow execution:
  - record an audit entry for each step action attempt (even if denied or failed)
  - include `step_id` / `step_name` / `workflow_name`
  - include policy decision and preconditions observed
  - include verification outcomes (wait-for matched, timeout)

- Redaction:
  - never store raw secrets or full inputs
  - store hashes/summaries consistent with the redaction system

- Correlation:
  - link audit entries to `workflow_execution_id`
  - link to the originating `event_id` when available

## Testing
- Integration tests:
  - run a synthetic workflow that attempts a send and a wait
  - verify audit timeline entries exist for both attempts and correlate to the workflow execution
- Redaction tests:
  - ensure the audit record never contains raw inputs/pane tails

## Acceptance Criteria
- A workflow run produces a coherent audit timeline that matches the workflow_step_log.
- Failures still produce audit entries that explain what was attempted and what was denied.

title: wa robot workflow - JSON workflow trigger/status/abort
description:
## Summary
Implement `wa robot workflow` commands that allow AI agents to trigger, monitor, and abort workflows programmatically via JSON interface.

## Background & Rationale
From PLAN.md Appendix A.2 Robot Commands:
```
wa robot workflow <name> <pane_id> [--force]
```

And from MCP tools (A.3):
```
wa.workflow_run - Execute workflow
```

AI agents need programmatic workflow control to:
1. Trigger workflows manually when auto-handling is disabled
2. Monitor workflow execution status
3. Abort stuck or unwanted workflows
4. Chain workflows based on results

This is the robot-mode interface to the workflow engine (wa-nu4.1.1).

## Implementation Details

### Command Structure
```bash
# Start a workflow
wa robot workflow start <name> <pane_id> [--force]
wa robot workflow start handle_compaction 3

# Check workflow status
wa robot workflow status [--workflow-id <id>] [--pane-id <pane>]

# Abort a running workflow
wa robot workflow abort <workflow-id> [--force]

# List available workflows
wa robot workflow list
```

### JSON Output Schema - Start
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "command": "workflow.start",
  "data": {
    "workflow_id": "wf-abc123",
    "workflow_name": "handle_compaction",
    "pane_id": 3,
    "status": "started",
    "started_at": "2025-01-18T10:30:00Z"
  }
}
```

### JSON Output Schema - Status
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "command": "workflow.status",
  "data": {
    "workflow_id": "wf-abc123",
    "workflow_name": "handle_compaction",
    "pane_id": 3,
    "status": "running",
    "current_step": 2,
    "total_steps": 5,
    "step_name": "wait_for_prompt",
    "started_at": "2025-01-18T10:30:00Z",
    "elapsed_ms": 5234
  }
}
```

### Error Cases (from Appendix B concepts)
- E_WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND: Workflow name doesn't exist
- E_WORKFLOW_LOCKED: Pane already has active workflow (unless --force)
- E_WORKFLOW_ABORTED: Workflow was aborted
- E_POLICY_DENIED: Policy engine denied workflow start
- E_PANE_NOT_FOUND: Target pane doesn't exist

### Implementation Notes
1. Integrate with workflow engine from wa-nu4.1.1.1
2. Respect per-pane workflow locks (wa-nu4.1.1.2)
3. Support --force to override locks (with audit)
4. Return workflow_id for subsequent status/abort calls
5. Include step-level progress for detailed monitoring

## Success Criteria
- [ ] `wa robot workflow start` triggers workflow and returns ID
- [ ] `wa robot workflow status` shows detailed progress
- [ ] `wa robot workflow abort` cleanly stops workflow
- [ ] `wa robot workflow list` shows available workflows
- [ ] --force overrides pane lock with audit
- [ ] Error codes are stable and actionable
- [ ] Unit tests for JSON serialization
- [ ] Integration test with mock workflow execution

## Dependencies
- wa-4vx.7.1 (robot scaffolding) - for JSON envelope and error codes
- wa-nu4.1.1.1 (workflow engine types) - for Workflow trait
- wa-nu4.1.1.2 (pane locks) - for lock management
- wa-nu4.1.1.5 (workflow runner) - for execution
close_reason: Duplicate/inapplicable: superseded by existing robot command beads (accounts: wa-nu4.1.5.4/wa-nu4.1.5.5; rules list/test: wa-nu4.2.1.4; robot workflow: wa-nu4.1.1.9).

title: Per-pane workflow lock/reservation (prevent conflicting automations)
description:
# Task: Per-pane workflow lock/reservation

## Goal
Ensure only one workflow runs per pane at a time (or per configurable lock class).

## Why
Without locks, multi-step workflows can interleave and inject nonsense into a terminal. Locks are the first line of correctness for any automation system.

## Scope boundary
This is an **internal workflow lock**, not the user-visible pane reservation system (see the separate pane reservations epic). It prevents workflow collisions even when no external reservation is set.

## Design (v0)
- In-memory lock table keyed by `pane_id`.
- Lock acquisition/release is recorded in workflow execution logs.
- Optional future: persisted lock record for multi-process/distributed mode (explicit non-goal for v0).

## Failure behavior
- If a lock cannot be acquired:
  - either skip starting the workflow (preferred)
  - or mark the event as “deferred / in_progress elsewhere” depending on event semantics

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - two concurrent start attempts for the same pane: exactly one acquires lock
  - lock is released on workflow completion and on abort

## Acceptance Criteria
- If a workflow is running on pane X, new detections for X do not start another workflow.
- Locks are released on both success and failure paths.

title: Persist workflow_executions + workflow_step_log; resume after restart from last completed step
description:
# Task: Persist workflow runs + resume logic

## Goal
Make workflows durable so `wa watch` can restart without losing where it was.

## Requirements
- On workflow start, create `workflow_executions` row.
- On each step:
  - mark step started with an input snapshot (redacted)
  - on completion mark completed with output snapshot (redacted)
  - on failure mark failed with error detail and attempt count
- On daemon restart:
  - find running/incomplete workflows
  - reconstruct state and resume from last completed step

## Idempotency notes
- Resuming must not repeat already-completed steps.
- Step results should be written before side effects whenever possible.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - resume computes next step index correctly given a step log
- Integration tests:
  - simulate “kill mid-workflow” and verify:
    - already-completed steps are not re-run
    - workflow completes after restart

## Acceptance Criteria
- Kill `wa watch` mid-workflow and restart: it resumes without repeating already-completed steps.
- Step logs are sufficient to understand what happened without consulting raw terminal text.
close_reason: done

title: WaitCondition implementation: Pattern wait + PaneIdle via OSC 133 (fallback heuristics if needed)
description:
# Task: WaitCondition implementation

## Goal
Implement `wait_for_condition` correctly, efficiently, and in a way that is shared across robot/workflow code paths.

This is one of the core reliability primitives:
- it’s how workflows avoid spamming
- it’s how workflows become resumable and debuggable
- it’s how “verified sends” become possible

## PaneIdle
Prefer deterministic shell integration:
- `PaneIdle` == observe OSC 133 prompt marker.

Fallback (only if shell integration missing):
- heuristic prompt match (explicitly marked as best-effort)

## Pattern wait
- Poll get-text (tail window) using the shared PaneWaiter (`wa-4vx.2.6`).
- Stop early on success.
- Return timeout error on deadline.

## Implementation notes
- Do not re-implement polling loops inside the workflow layer; reuse PaneWaiter so:
  - workflow waits, robot wait-for, and send verification behave identically
  - backoff and cancellation semantics are consistent

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - Pattern wait succeeds/fails deterministically on synthetic fixtures.
  - Timeouts are honored precisely (no “wait forever” bugs).
  - Cancellation produces a stable outcome and a debuggable step log entry.
  - PaneIdle transitions are correct for OSC 133 sequences.
  - Fallback heuristics are only used when deterministic signals are missing (and are clearly reported).

- Integration tests:
  - A synthetic workflow run that includes at least one wait step records stable step logs and does not spam sends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- WaitFor works reliably on synthetic fixtures.
- Timeouts/cancellations produce stable, debuggable step logs.
notes: WaitCondition implementation complete: WaitConditionExecutor handles Pattern and PaneIdle conditions with OSC 133 deterministic detection and heuristic fallback. Fixed false positive bug in heuristic_idle_check that matched 'Progress: 50%' as prompt. All 9 WaitCondition tests pass including pane_idle with OSC133, heuristics fallback, timeout behavior, and pattern matching.

title: Workflow runner: consume Detection events, select workflow, execute with policy gates
description:
# Task: Workflow runner/scheduler

## Goal
Bridge between detections/events and workflow executions.

## Responsibilities
- Subscribe to detection/event stream.
- Choose the highest-priority matching workflow.
- Enforce per-pane lock.
- Execute steps with:
  - policy checks before any input injection
  - bounded retries with backoff
  - step logging (durable)
  - clear “why did/didn’t we act?” outcomes

## Action execution architecture (important)
To avoid duplicated safety logic, the runner should not “roll its own” injection path. It should route any action attempt (send text, ctrl-c, etc) through a shared core helper that:
- calls PolicyEngine
- emits audit entries (when wired)
- performs the action only if allowed

This is how we ensure robot/human/workflow paths stay consistent.

## Event interaction
- The runner should cooperate with event semantics (`wa-nu4.1.1.10`):
  - set `in_progress` (if used)
  - mark handled on completion/abort/failure
  - avoid spamming repeat executions for the same event

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - workflow selection chooses correct workflow given a detection
  - lock prevents concurrent runs per pane
  - policy-denied action yields a stable denied outcome without calling send
- Integration tests:
  - synthetic event stream → creates workflow_executions + step logs

## Acceptance Criteria
- When a compaction detection arrives, `handle_compaction` workflow runs and records a completed execution.
- When policy denies an action, the workflow records an explainable denied/aborted result and does not inject input.

title: Data-driven workflow descriptors (YAML/TOML) for simple prompt injection sequences
description:
# Task: Data-driven workflow descriptors (YAML/TOML)

## Goal
Allow operator customization of **simple, safe workflows** without recompiling wa.

This is about *configuration-driven prompt sequences* ("wait for X, then send Y"), not complex logic.

## Scope (strict)
Only support a small, explicitly safe step vocabulary:
- `wait_for` (substring/regex) with timeout
- `sleep` (bounded)
- `send_text` (must go through PolicyEngine; can be denied)
- `send_ctrl` (limited set like Ctrl-C; also policy gated)

Non-goals:
- loops/conditionals
- arbitrary shell execution
- custom code hooks

## Descriptor model
- Versioned schema (e.g., `workflow_schema_version: 1`).
- Strong validation at load time:
  - unknown fields rejected
  - timeouts and sleep durations bounded
  - maximum number of steps bounded
  - step ids unique for audit/logging

## Execution integration
- Descriptors compile into the same internal step executor used by Rust workflows.
- Every send step uses the shared policy-gated injection helper.

title: Integrate workflow action loop into `wa watch` (auto-handle) while preserving observe/act split
description:
# Task: Integrate workflows into `wa watch`

## Goal
Enable `wa watch --auto-handle` to run workflows in response to detections, while keeping the **observe** loop strictly passive and the **act** loop explicitly gated.

This is the moment `wa` stops being “just a recorder/search index” and becomes a safe automation runtime.

## Core invariants (non-negotiable)
- The observation loop remains passive:
  - no `send-text`, no control sequences, no workflow actions
  - if workflow code is not enabled, wa still captures + indexes reliably
- The action loop is explicit:
  - runs only when enabled by config/flags
  - always re-checks live pane state immediately before each action
  - every action attempt is policy-gated

## Deliverables
- `wa watch` starts a workflow runner/scheduler when configured.
- Config + flags:
  - enable/disable workflow runtime
  - allowlist which workflows may auto-run
  - max concurrent workflows (global + per-pane)
  - `--auto-handle` (opt-in) to act automatically
- Structured logs and audit correlation:
  - a workflow execution id is included on all logs for that run

## Failure and safety behavior
- If policy denies an action during a workflow:
  - workflow step is recorded as denied (not retried blindly)
  - the originating event remains visible to the user/robot as unhandled (or handled_aborted, depending on semantics in `wa-nu4.1.1.10`)
- If workflow engine errors:
  - observation loop continues running
  - action loop stops cleanly and reports an actionable error

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - workflow runner does not start when `--auto-handle` is off
  - action loop does not execute without explicit enable
- Integration tests:
  - given a synthetic detection stream, `wa watch` launches workflow execution and records execution rows
  - denied policy decisions never result in a send attempt
- E2E:
  - `wa-4vx.10.8` compaction workflow end-to-end
  - `wa-4vx.10.9` usage-limit workflow end-to-end
  - `wa-4vx.10.12` restart/resume idempotency

## Acceptance Criteria
- With `--auto-handle` enabled and compaction is detected, the workflow triggers exactly once per event (subject to dedupe/cooldown semantics).
- With `--auto-handle` disabled, detections/events are recorded but no sends occur.
- A denied policy decision prevents any input injection and produces a stable, explainable result (logs + audit/step log).

title: [EPIC] Workflow: handle_compaction (safe context reinjection)
description:
# Workflow: handle_compaction

## Goal
When an agent compacts its context, automatically re-inject the minimal prompt that restores critical project context.

## Why
Compaction causes the agent to forget important constraints (safety rules, repo conventions, current objectives). A deterministic, immediate prompt keeps agent behavior aligned without relying on “human noticing”.

## Core behavior (PLAN Appendix D.1; made self-contained)
- Trigger: detection event `session.compaction`.
- Each step follows the invariant: **Observe → Act → Verify**.

### Step plan (v0)
1. Acquire per-pane workflow lock.
2. Re-read current pane tail (defensive: guard against stale detections).
3. Guard: ensure the compaction anchor is still present within the last N lines.
4. Guard: abort if pane is `AltScreen` (vim/less/etc.) unless explicitly allowed by config.
5. Guard: abort if we have a `RecentGap`/`OutputGap` (state is uncertain).
6. Stabilize:
   - wait a short stabilization window (default: 2s), OR
   - require a deterministic “compaction complete” marker if/when we have one.
7. Send agent-specific prompt (exact strings; include the trailing newline):
   - Claude Code: `"Reread AGENTS.md so it's still fresh in your mind.\n"`
   - Codex: `"Please re-read AGENTS.md and any key project context files.\n"`
   - Gemini: `"Please re-examine AGENTS.md and project context.\n"`
8. Verify:
   - prefer deterministic markers (OSC 133 prompt boundary) if available
   - otherwise accept a minimal verification (prompt echo / UI marker) and record what was observed
9. Mark event handled and record workflow result + step logs.

### Failure modes (v0)
- Pane disappeared: mark workflow cancelled (do not retry blindly).
- Alt-screen detected: abort safely (unless explicitly allowed).
- Verification timeout: mark failed/paused with a next-step plan (do not spam retries).

## Safety
- Never send into alt-screen.
- All sends are PolicyEngine-gated (PromptActive/AgentWaiting, no gaps, rate limits).
- Rate-limited + deduped via event semantics (no prompt spam).


## Success Criteria
- Compaction events are detected and translated into workflow executions safely (policy-gated, deduped).
- Workflow prompts are agent-specific, idempotent, and leave an audit + step-log trail.
- Guards prevent sending when pane state is uncertain (alt-screen, recent gaps, missing anchor).


## Testing
- Unit/integration tests:
  - Synthetic compaction detection triggers exactly one workflow run and exactly one send.
  - Guards:
    - refuses to act when AltScreen or RecentGap is present
    - refuses to act when compaction anchor is no longer visible
  - Stabilization: does not send before the stabilization condition is met.

- E2E:
  - End-to-end compaction scenario covered with full artifacts via `wa-4vx.10.8`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.
close_reason: done

description:
# Task: Implement HandleCompaction workflow

## Goal
Ship a safe, deterministic workflow that reacts to compaction events by prompting the agent to refresh critical context.

This is the concrete implementation of PLAN Appendix D.1.

## Trigger
- Detection event `session.compaction` (from the relevant agent pack).

## Step plan (Observe → Act → Verify)
1. Acquire per-pane workflow lock.
2. Re-read pane tail to confirm the compaction anchor is still present (avoid acting on stale detections).
3. Guard: abort if pane is `AltScreen` or we have a recent output gap (`OutputGap`/`RecentGap`).
4. Stabilize (see `wa-nu4.1.2.2`):
   - wait a short stabilization window (default: 2s), OR
   - require a deterministic marker if we have one.
5. Send agent-specific refresh prompt (exact strings; include trailing newline):
   - Claude Code: `"Reread AGENTS.md so it's still fresh in your mind.\n"`
   - Codex: `"Please re-read AGENTS.md and any key project context files.\n"`
   - Gemini: `"Please re-examine AGENTS.md and project context.\n"`
6. Verify send:
   - prefer deterministic verification via OSC 133 prompt boundary after the send
   - otherwise accept prompt echo/agent UI marker as best-effort
   - on timeout: mark the workflow `paused` with a “next steps” payload (do not spam retries)
7. Record workflow result + mark event handled.

## Safety
- All sends are policy-gated.
- Rate limiting applies.
- Workflow is idempotent: repeated compaction detections should not spam prompts (dedupe/cooldown semantics apply).

## Failure modes (must be handled explicitly)
- Pane disappeared: cancel workflow.
- Policy denies send: record denied/aborted result; do not inject input.
- Verification timeout: pause with a next-step plan; keep the event visible but not “unhandled spam”.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - guards behave correctly (alt-screen/gap → abort)
  - anchor confirmation avoids acting when the anchor disappears
- Integration tests:
  - synthetic detection → one execution → event marked handled
  - “policy denied” path records denial and sends nothing
- E2E:
  - `wa-4vx.10.8` validates end-to-end behavior with verbose artifacts

## Acceptance Criteria
- When the compaction anchor appears in a pane, wa sends the prompt once and records a handled event.
- If policy denies, the workflow records a denied/aborted result and does not inject input.

# Task: Compaction stabilization strategy

## Goal
Avoid racing the agent UI while compaction is finishing.

If we send a “refresh”/context reinjection prompt too early, the agent may still be streaming UI updates and miss the instruction.

## Options
- Simple: wait a small fixed window (e.g., 1–2s) after detection.
- Better: wait until tail lines stop changing for N polls.
- Best: use deterministic signal (user-var) if the agent emits one.

## Deliverables
- Implement one strategy now (likely stable tail window).
- Keep the design extensible for future deterministic markers.

## Testing
- Unit/integration tests (see `wa-nu4.1.2.4`):
  - stabilization waits the intended condition (stable tail or marker)
  - does not wait forever (hard timeout)
  - does not spam get-text excessively (bounded polling)
- E2E:
  - `wa-4vx.10.8` validates compaction workflow end-to-end with dummy pane + logs

# Workflow: handle_usage_limits (Codex-first)

## Goal
Respond to usage-limit reached events deterministically:
- ensure session is paused safely
- capture/resume metadata (session id, token usage)

- persist a structured "next steps" record

## Safety constraints
- all sends are PolicyEngine-gated

- Failover (when enabled) selects an account deterministically, completes device auth safely, and resumes the prior session.
- If interactive auth is required, the system fails safely with a clear next-step plan and artifacts.

title: Codex usage-limit workflow spec as executable step plan (guards, verify markers, failure modes)
description:
# Task: Codex usage-limit workflow spec (executable)

## Goal
Write the step-by-step plan as a concrete, executable workflow specification so implementation stays aligned.

This task exists because usage-limit handling is:
- multi-step
- safety-sensitive (input injection + browser automation)
- prone to drift if not pinned to explicit invariants

## Canonical trigger + preconditions
- Trigger event: `usage.reached` (Codex pack), with inferred agent = `codex`.
- Preconditions (must be checked before *every* send):
  - pane is not `AltScreen`
  - pane has no recent `OutputGap`
  - PolicyEngine authorizes `SendText` / `BrowserAuth` for the current step

## Canonical step plan (PLAN Appendix D.2; Observe → Act → Verify)
1. Acquire per-pane lock.

2. Exit Codex cleanly (avoid fixed sleeps):
   - Act: send Ctrl-C once (`\u{3}` / byte `0x03`).
   - Verify: wait for session summary / resume hint markers.
   - If not seen within a short grace window, Act: send Ctrl-C again.
   - Verify: continue waiting (bounded by overall timeout) until summary/resume markers appear.

   Rationale: this is more deterministic than “sleep 200ms”, and reduces unnecessary double-interrupts.

3. Verify session summary/resume hint appears (PaneWaiter; bounded tail; timeout).
4. Parse:
   - token usage stats (total/input/cached/output/reasoning) from the summary
   - resume session id from the resume hint

5. Refresh account usage out-of-band (not in the pane):
   - `caut refresh --service openai --format json`
   - persist/update the local accounts mirror

6. Select account:
   - choose highest `percent_remaining` above threshold
   - tie-breaker: LRU last_used
   - if none above threshold: branch to “failover disabled / pause” below

7. Initiate device auth in the Codex pane:
   - Act: send `cod login --device-auth\n`
   - Verify: device code prompt appears

8. Parse device code (and URL if present) from the pane tail.

9. Playwright: complete device auth flow (persistent profile for the chosen account).

10. Resume session:
   - Act: send `cod resume <session_id>\n`
   - Verify: “ready” marker / prompt appears

11. Wait for “ready” marker (PaneWaiter; timeout).

12. Continue:
   - Act: send `proceed.\n`
   - Verify: Codex begins responding (or an agreed marker appears)

13. Persist:
   - mark event handled
   - store session info + account rotation record + workflow step logs

## Failure modes + explicit handling (v0)
- Device code not found:
  - retry step 7 once
  - if still missing: pause with next-step plan (do not loop)

- Playwright cannot proceed (MFA or unexpected auth wall):
  - open non-headless browser and request human completion
  - pause the workflow and persist the recovery instructions (profile path, URL)

- Resume fails (session id invalid / resume rejected):
  - surface error details; do not loop

- Pane state becomes unsafe mid-flow (AltScreen/OutputGap/CommandRunning):
  - abort/pause safely and record why

## Variant: failover disabled / safe pause
If failover (account rotation + browser automation) is disabled by config, OR step 6 cannot pick an account:
- Do **not** attempt `cod login`.
- Persist a redacted next-step plan including:
  - try-again time (from `codex.usage.reached` if available)
  - resume session id (redacted/hashed)
  - recommended human actions
- Mark event as `paused` (so it does not reappear as “unhandled spam”).

## Testing guidance (for downstream implementers)
These are required fixtures/fixtures-to-corpus so implementation is deterministic:
- “usage limit reached” output
- session summary (tokens + resume hint)
- device auth prompt output (device code)
- resume output (“ready” markers)

## Acceptance Criteria
- The spec covers both failover-enabled and failover-disabled paths.
- Every step has:
  - explicit inputs/outputs
  - verification strategy
  - explicit safe failure behavior
  - timeouts + retry policy (even if initial values are conservative)
close_reason: Spec complete in bead description; downstream implementation tasks defined

title: Implement step: exit Codex gracefully (Ctrl-C x2) and wait for session summary

# Task: Exit Codex gracefully (Ctrl-C) and capture session summary

## Goal
On usage limit reached, terminate the Codex interactive session in a way that reliably produces the session summary:
- token usage
- resume hint / session id

This step is the foundation for safe resume/failover because it extracts the canonical state from Codex itself.

## Actions (robust; avoid fixed sleeps)
Instead of always doing “Ctrl-C twice + sleep”, do a **bounded, observation-driven** sequence:

1) Send Ctrl-C once (byte `0x03`).
2) Observe/verify: use PaneWaiter to wait for the session-summary marker(s).
3) If the summary markers do not appear within a short grace window, send Ctrl-C again.
4) Continue waiting (bounded by an overall timeout) until summary markers appear.

This aligns with the project invariant “deterministic over probabilistic”: we don’t assume 200ms is enough; we wait for observable state.

## Verification
- Use shared wait logic (`PaneWaiter`) to wait for a session-summary marker.
- Minimum acceptable markers (allow drift):
  - `Token usage:`
  - `To continue this session, run codex resume` (or equivalent “resume hint” anchor)

## Safety / policy
- Any input injection must be policy-gated.
- If policy denies (alt-screen, recent gap, etc): abort this step with an actionable reason; do not retry blindly.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - marker detection succeeds and returns a stable “summary seen” result
  - timeout produces a stable error including elapsed + last-seen tail hash (not raw content)
  - “second Ctrl-C only when needed”: if the fixture shows summary after first Ctrl-C, ensure we do not inject the second

- Integration tests:
  - given a fixture transcript with session summary, the step extracts the expected markers and produces a parseable output for the next step

## Acceptance Criteria

- If the summary marker does not appear within timeout, the step fails with an actionable error and produces safe debug context (no raw secrets).

title: Safe fallback path: failover disabled or MFA blocks → pause + persist next-step plan
description:
# Task: Safe fallback path (failover disabled / NeedsHuman / MFA blocks)

## Goal
When full account failover cannot be completed, the system must fail **safe** and still be **useful**:
- do not loop or spam the pane
- persist what happened and what to do next
- make the paused state visible to both humans and agents

This is a user-trust critical path: it’s the difference between “wa is safe” and “wa is a runaway bot”.

## Trigger conditions (examples)
Enter fallback when:
- failover is disabled by config
- browser auth returns `NeedsHuman` (password/MFA/SSO)
- required external tools are missing (`caut`, Playwright, etc.)
- policy prevents safe injection (alt-screen, recent gap, unknown state)

## Behavior
### Stop attempting automation
- Do **not** continue injecting input after the blocking condition.
- Ensure the workflow runner marks the event as **paused** (per `wa-nu4.1.1.10`) so it does not re-run automatically.

### Persist a structured next-step plan
Persist a redacted “next step plan” payload (in step logs and/or event metadata) that includes:
- what happened (high-level)
- what is required from the operator (explicit steps)
- when it is safe to retry (reset time if known)
- identifiers needed to resume:
  - resume session id (if available)
  - which account/profile was being used (non-secret identifier)

### Surface the plan
- `wa robot events` and `wa events` must show:
  - status: paused
  - next steps (redacted)
  - suggested command(s) to resume or re-run manually (if applicable)

## Safety / privacy
- Never store secrets in plaintext.
- Any URL/code that could contain tokens must be redacted before persistence.
- Store hashes/summaries instead of raw codes.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - next-step plan generation is deterministic and redacts sensitive substrings
  - paused events are excluded from `--unhandled` by default
- Integration tests:
  - synthetic usage-limit workflow run hits fallback → event becomes paused with next-step plan
- E2E:
  - `wa-4vx.10.9` validates the safe pause/restart-plan path with verbose artifacts

## Acceptance Criteria
- Operator can query events and recover using the next-step plan without consulting `PLAN.md`.
- The system fails safe: no repeated input injection attempts when automation cannot proceed.

title: [EPIC] Browser automation skeleton (Playwright profiles + OpenAI device auth)
description:
# Browser automation skeleton

## Goal
Provide the minimal browser automation required for Codex/OpenAI device auth.

## Design principles
- Prefer persistent browser profiles over stored passwords.
- Never log secrets.
- If Playwright hits MFA/password, fall back to interactive completion and then persist profile.



## Success Criteria
- Playwright-based browser automation supports persistent profiles and safe logging/artifacts.
- OpenAI device auth flow works for already-authenticated profiles and fails safely for MFA/password-required cases.
- A smoke-test command exists to validate browser automation on a real machine without embedding secrets.


## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - URL matching + state-machine transitions for the device-auth flow.
  - Redaction tests: ensure device codes / tokens never appear in logs or artifacts.

- Manual smoke test (required):
  - Provide a dedicated `wa browser smoke-test ...` command (see `wa-nu4.1.4.4`) that:
    - validates Playwright can launch with the configured profile dir
    - validates it can reach the device auth page
    - reports exactly what step failed with an artifact bundle

- Negative-path tests:
  - Explicitly exercise MFA/password-required cases and assert we fail safe with clear next steps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

title: Implement OpenAI/Codex device auth flow (auth.openai.com/codex/device)
description:
# Task: OpenAI device auth flow (Playwright)

## Goal
Automate the OpenAI device-code flow used by Codex CLI via Playwright in a way that is:
- robust to small UI changes
- safe with respect to secrets (no password storage)
- debuggable when it fails (screenshots/HTML dumps, redacted logs)

Target URL:
- `https://auth.openai.com/codex/device`

## Preconditions / inputs
- A persistent Playwright profile exists for the target account (profile dir derived from workspace/config).
- The workflow step has already obtained a `user_code` (device code) from the Codex pane.

## Happy path (v0)
1. Navigate to the device page.
2. Ensure we are in a logged-in state for the intended account:
   - if already logged in: proceed
   - if email prompt appears: fill email, continue
   - if password/MFA required: **do not attempt to automate**; exit into the fallback path (`wa-nu4.1.4.3`)
3. Fill the `user_code` form field.
4. Submit.
5. Verify success via a stable marker:
   - preferred: page contains “Successfully logged in” (or equivalent stable selector)
   - also capture URL + final DOM snapshot for debugging

## Failure modes
- Password/MFA prompts:
  - return a structured error that the workflow can treat as “interactive bootstrap required”
  - point to the fallback task (`wa-nu4.1.4.3`)
- Rate limit / bot detection / unexpected page:
  - fail with actionable error and attach redacted artifacts

## Logging / artifacts
- Never log passwords, session cookies, access tokens, or raw HTML that may contain secrets.
- On failure, write artifacts under the workspace artifacts dir:
  - screenshot
  - redacted DOM snapshot (or a hash + minimal selector debug)
  - a short, human-readable failure report

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - parse + validate the `user_code` format before browser automation (fail fast)
- Integration tests (offline):
  - run Playwright against a local HTML fixture that simulates the device page, verifying selector strategy
- Manual smoke tests:
  - a `wa browser smoke-test --openai-device` (tracked elsewhere) confirms it can complete on a real profile

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a valid persistent profile that is already authenticated, this flow completes and returns “success” for a real account.
- If password/MFA is required, the flow exits safely with a clear “interactive bootstrap required” error and produces redacted artifacts.

title: Profile persistence + MFA/password fallback (one-time interactive bootstrap)
description:
# Task: Profile persistence + MFA fallback

## Goal
Make auth reliable in the real world where MFA exists.

## Strategy
- Prefer persistent profiles so most auth runs require no credential entry.
- If Playwright detects password/MFA prompts:
  - open interactive browser window
  - prompt the operator to complete login once
  - then persist storage state for future automated runs

## Safety
- Never store passwords.
- Never log raw MFA codes, cookies, or OAuth redirect URLs with sensitive params.

## Testing
- Manual test plan:
  - first run requires interactive bootstrap
  - subsequent runs succeed without password prompts

## Acceptance Criteria
- After one interactive bootstrap, subsequent runs succeed without password prompts.

title: Browser smoke-test command (manual) + failure reporting conventions
description:
# Task: Browser smoke-test command (manual)

## Goal
Provide a simple, human-invokable command to validate Playwright integration **outside** full workflows.

When selectors change (which they will), we want a fast feedback loop:
- run one command
- get a precise failure
- fix the automation

## Proposed CLI surface
- `wa auth test openai --account <name>`
  - exercises the OpenAI/Codex device auth flow end-to-end

- Optional flags:
  - `--profile <name>` (select persistent browser profile)
  - `--timeout-secs <n>`
  - `--headful` (default headless; headful for debugging)

## Output & error conventions
- Always return a structured outcome **matching the auth realities matrix** (`wa-nu4.1.4.5`):
  - `Success` → maps to `Automated`
  - `NeedsHuman` → maps to `NeedsHuman`
  - `Failed` → maps to `Fail`

- Failure output must include:
  - which step failed
  - current page URL (redacted)
  - recommended next action (update selector, run headful, etc.)

## Safety requirements
- Never ask for or store passwords.
- Redact URLs containing tokens/codes in logs.
- Always close contexts/pages on all code paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running the command either succeeds or returns a precise error with next steps.
- Outcome categories are consistent with the auth realities matrix (no new ad-hoc states).
- Errors are stable and actionable (not vague “something failed”).


## Testing
- Manual test plan:
  - Run headless + headful modes.
  - Validate all three outcomes are reachable in controlled conditions:
    - Success (already-authenticated profile)
    - NeedsHuman (profile not authenticated / MFA)
    - Failed (simulate selector mismatch)

- Redaction tests:
  - Ensure logs/artifacts do not contain device codes or tokenized URLs.

title: Auth realities matrix — OpenAI/Codex
description:
# Task: Auth realities matrix — OpenAI/Codex

## Goal
Establish a **factual, repeatable** understanding of which OpenAI/Codex auth paths can be fully automated and which require a one-time human bootstrap.

This resolves PLAN.md Open Question #3 for the OpenAI/Codex path and prevents workflows from guessing.

## Why this matters (user value)
When a pane hits usage limits, wa must decide whether to:
- proceed automatically, or
- pause and request a human action

A documented matrix avoids brittle heuristics and makes failures explainable.

## Scope
- OpenAI/Codex device auth flow only (Phase 2).
- Manual exploration of **real-world states** and how to detect them:
  - already authenticated profile
  - needs device code entry
  - MFA/password required
  - SSO/enterprise redirect
  - rate-limited / captcha
- Outcome taxonomy to standardize across automation:
  - `Automated`
  - `NeedsHuman`
  - `Fail`

## Deliverables
1. **Auth realities matrix** (checked into docs or spec notes):
   - state name
   - detection signals (selectors / URLs / CLI prompts)
   - automation outcome (`Automated`, `NeedsHuman`, `Fail`)
   - required human steps (if any)
   - safe retry guidance

2. **Outcome taxonomy + workflow guidance**:
   - how `handle_usage_limits` should message `NeedsHuman`
   - how PolicyEngine should respond when auth is not automatable

3. **Redaction rules**:
   - define what must be scrubbed in auth artifacts (device codes, tokenized URLs)

> Note: Smoke-test alignment against this matrix is tracked in `wa-nu4.1.4.4`.

## Testing / validation (manual)
- Run manual auth checks in controlled scenarios:
  - already-authenticated profile → `Automated`
  - fresh profile → `NeedsHuman`
  - forced MFA/SSO (if available) → `NeedsHuman`

- Redaction checks:
  - notes/artifacts must not contain device codes or auth tokens

## Acceptance Criteria
- A documented matrix exists for **all OpenAI/Codex auth states** observed during testing.
- The outcome taxonomy is explicit and referenced by workflow fallback text.
- Redaction rules are written and unambiguous.

# Accounts + usage integration

## Goal
Integrate `caut` (coding_agent_usage_tracker) so wa can make quota-aware decisions.

## Core idea
`caut` is the usage truth; wa mirrors data for history and selection.

## Deliverables

- selection policy: highest percent remaining + LRU tie-break
- persistence to accounts table



## Success Criteria
- `caut` integration provides typed usage/account data and maps errors into actionable UX.
- Account selection is deterministic (threshold + LRU tie-break) and explainable.
- DB mirror supports listing/previewing selection decisions in robot/human surfaces.
- Unit/integration tests cover parsing, selection determinism, and DB updates.


## Testing

  - JSON parsing fixtures for `caut usage` and `caut refresh` outputs (including partial/malformed outputs and stderr noise).
  - Selection determinism tests (tie-breakers, thresholds, LRU updates).

- Integration tests:
  - Use a fake/fixture `caut` implementation to exercise the wrapper without hitting real accounts.
  - Verify DB mirror updates and robot/human views never expose secrets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.

title: Implement caut wrapper (usage/refresh JSON parsing, error mapping)
description:
# Task: caut wrapper (usage/refresh)

## Goal
Treat `caut` as the authoritative usage/account source and expose a small internal API that:
- invokes `caut` safely (timeouts, error capture)
- parses its JSON output into typed Rust structs
- maps failures into actionable, user-friendly errors

## Why
wa should not re-implement remote API logic that already exists in `caut`. The wrapper is the “stability layer” between:
- `wa` workflows/robots that need usage data
- the external `caut` CLI which can drift slightly in output format

## Scope
- Supported subcommands (v0):
  - `caut usage --service <svc> --format json`
  - `caut refresh --service <svc> --format json`
- Supported services (initial): `openai` (extend later)

## Design
- Provide a wrapper module that:
  - builds the command line
  - executes with a hard timeout
  - captures stdout/stderr
  - limits output size
  - parses JSON with `serde`
- Error mapping:
  - `caut` missing: actionable install hint
  - non-zero exit: include stderr summary (bounded)
  - invalid JSON: include a small redacted preview + version info if available

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - parse known-good fixtures
  - parse edge-case fixtures (missing fields, new fields, commas in numbers)
  - validate that unknown fields do not break parsing if possible
  - error mapping behavior (missing binary, timeout, invalid json)
- Integration tests:
  - a small “fake caut” test binary/script in tests (or dependency injection) to simulate exit codes and stderr

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a sample `caut` JSON fixture (usage + refresh), parsing succeeds and produces a stable typed representation.
- Failures (missing binary, timeout, invalid JSON) produce actionable errors without panics and without logging secrets.
close_reason: Verified complete by BrightCrane: CautClient wrapper with 5 passing tests

title: Account selection policy (percent remaining + LRU) + persistence mirror in accounts table
description:
# Task: Account selection policy + persistence

## Goal
Given current usage info (from `caut`), select the best account for failover and persist enough state to make the choice:
- deterministic
- explainable
- resistant to thrashing

## Policy (v0)
- Primary: highest `percent_remaining`.
- Filter: exclude accounts below a configured threshold (avoid selecting accounts that will immediately fail).
- Tie-breaker: least-recently-used (`last_used_at` oldest wins).

## Persistence model
- Mirror current usage into an `accounts` table (history optional; can be added later).
- Store at least:
  - account identifier (stable id or email hash)
  - service (openai, later others)
  - percent_remaining
  - reset_at / next_reset_at (if available)
  - last_refreshed_at
  - last_used_at (updated only after a successful failover)

## Explainability
- Selection output should include a short explanation for logging/audit:
  - which accounts were considered
  - which were filtered and why
  - which tie-breaker applied

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - deterministic selection on fixed fixture inputs
  - threshold filtering
  - tie-breaker correctness
  - stable behavior when fields are missing (e.g., no reset time)
- Integration tests:
  - DB mirror updates are correct (insert/update)
  - `last_used_at` only updates after a “success” signal from the workflow

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a fixed fixture of accounts + usage, selection is deterministic and stable.
- Accounts below threshold are never selected.
- `accounts.last_used_at` updates only after a successful failover path.
close_reason: Verified complete by BrightCrane: 9 passing tests for account selection policy

title: Accounts tests: caut parsing + selection determinism + DB mirror updates
description:
# Task: Accounts tests

## Goal
Prevent quota/rotation regressions by locking down accounts parsing + selection behavior.

This is critical because a small bug here can cause:
- thrashing between accounts
- using a depleted account repeatedly
- mis-reporting usage

## Fixture strategy
- Store `caut` output fixtures (stdout) for multiple scenarios:
  - multiple accounts with different remaining quotas
  - tie cases (same percent remaining)
  - missing/partial fields
  - “service unavailable” / error output

## What to validate
- Parsing:
  - fixtures parse deterministically
  - errors are structured and actionable (no panics)

- Selection policy:
  - threshold filtering works (ignore accounts below min remaining)
  - tie-breakers are deterministic (LRU / last-used / stable order)
  - “preferred account” override (if supported) is respected

- Persistence mirror:
  - parsed account state is mirrored into the DB accounts table
  - updates are idempotent
  - timestamps/last_used update rules are correct

## Testing approach
- Unit tests for parse + selection logic.
- Integration tests using a temp DB for mirror updates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Accounts parsing + selection is deterministic on fixtures.
- DB mirror update behavior is covered by integration tests.
- Error fixtures do not cause panics and produce clear diagnostics.

title: [EPIC] Pane reservations (exclusive/TTL) for safe multi-step work
description:
# [EPIC] Pane reservations (exclusive/TTL) for safe multi-step work

## Mission
Provide a first-class, auditable way to reserve a pane for exclusive use during multi-step operations.

## Why this matters
User story A6 requires a deterministic lock so:
- a workflow or agent can perform multiple steps without interference
- humans and other agents can see *who owns a pane* and why
- automation avoids "cross-talk" between overlapping operations

## Scope
- A reservation model with TTL and owner identity.
- Enforcement in policy/send paths (deny or require approval when a pane is reserved by someone else).
- Robot + human commands to acquire/release/list reservations.
- Visibility in `wa status` and `wa robot state`.

## Non-goals
- Cross-machine coordination (handled in distributed mode).
- Long-lived leases without TTL (all reservations must expire).

## Success Criteria
- Reservations prevent accidental interference without blocking necessary manual intervention.
- Locks are visible and auditable (who/why/when/TTL).
- All automation paths respect reservations by default.

## Testing
- Unit tests for lease creation, expiry, and conflict behavior.
- Integration tests for policy enforcement.
- E2E scenario with artifacts showing reserve → action → release.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.
close_reason: done

title: Reservation model + storage schema (pane_reservations) + expiry
description:
# Task: Reservation model + storage schema

## Goal
Define and persist pane reservations with TTL and owner metadata.

## Data model (suggested)
Table `pane_reservations`:
- `id`
- `pane_id`
- `owner_kind` (human|robot|workflow|mcp)
- `owner_id` (string: session id / agent id / workflow id)
- `reason` (short string)
- `created_at`
- `expires_at`
- `released_at` (nullable)
- `status` (active|expired|released)

## Semantics
- Only one active reservation per pane.
- Reservations auto-expire on TTL; expiry is treated as release.
- **Config defaults**:
  - default TTL
  - maximum TTL
  - conflict behavior (deny vs require-approval)

## Deliverables
- Schema migration + indexes (`pane_id`, `status`, `expires_at`).
- Storage API:
  - create reservation
  - release reservation
  - list active reservations
  - expire stale reservations

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - cannot create a second active reservation for same pane
  - expiry logic moves reservation to expired
  - TTL bounds enforced from config defaults
- Integration tests:
  - reserve → release updates DB correctly

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reservations persist and expire deterministically.
- Queries for active reservations are fast and correct.
- Default TTL policy is enforced and documented.

title: Enforce reservations in PolicyEngine + send paths
description:
# Task: Enforce reservations in PolicyEngine + send paths

## Goal
Prevent unintended input injection into panes owned by someone else.

## Behavior
- PolicyEngine checks active reservation for the target pane.
- If reservation exists and owner != caller:
  - default: `RequireApproval` (human) or structured denial (robot/mcp)
  - include reservation metadata (owner, reason, expires_at) in the decision
- If caller is the owner, allow as normal.

## Integration points
- `wa robot send`
- `wa send`
- workflow step runner
- future MCP tools

## Audit
- Every reservation-based denial is recorded in audit trail (redacted).

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - owner can act
  - non-owner denied or requires approval
  - expired reservation treated as no reservation
- Integration tests:
  - policy decisions are stable and include reservation info

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reservations are consistently enforced across all action paths.
- Robot/MCP errors are stable and machine-parseable.
close_reason: done

title: Robot/Human commands: reserve/release/list pane reservations
description:
# Task: Robot/Human commands for pane reservations

## Goal
Expose a clear API to acquire/release reservations and inspect who owns a pane.

## Robot mode (stable JSON)
- `wa robot reserve <pane_id> --ttl <secs> --reason <text>`
- `wa robot release <pane_id>`
- `wa robot reservations` (list active)

## Human CLI
- `wa reserve <pane_id> --ttl ...` (alias or subcommand)
- `wa reservations` (table view)

## UX requirements
- Errors must be explicit:
  - already reserved
  - reservation expired
  - invalid TTL
- Output includes:
  - owner
  - reason
  - expires_at

## Safety
- `reserve` / `release` must pass PolicyEngine (`ActionKind::ReservePane/ReleasePane`).
- Policy can require approval for reservations if configured.

## Integration
- `wa status` and `wa robot state` should surface reservation state for each pane.

## Testing
- Unit tests for command parsing and validation.
- Integration tests for reserve → list → release lifecycle.
- Policy tests: deny/require-approval for reserve/release when rules demand.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reservations can be created, inspected, and released via robot + human commands.
- Outputs are stable and documented in the robot schema.

title: Tests/E2E: pane reservations (TTL, conflicts, audit)
description:
# Task: Tests/E2E — pane reservations

## Goal
Prove reservation behavior is correct, enforced, and visible with strong artifacts.

## Unit/integration tests
- Reserve → conflict → release lifecycle.
- TTL expiry converts active reservation to expired.
- Policy enforcement returns stable error codes and reasons.

## E2E scenario
- Reserve a pane via `wa robot reserve`.
- Attempt to send from a different owner (expect deny/require-approval).
- Release reservation and send again (expect allow).

## Artifacts
- Structured logs
- Audit trail extract (redacted)
- JSON outputs for robot commands

## Registry
- Register this case in the E2E case registry (`wa-4vx.10.20`), including prerequisites and default inclusion status.
- Ensure `./scripts/e2e_test.sh --all` includes this case (or mark non-default with justification).

## Logging
- Follow the standard E2E harness logging contract (`wa-4vx.10.6`) and runner (`wa-4vx.10.11`).
- Emit per-step start/end markers with timestamps + durations.
- Include case name and pane ids in every log line.
- Redact secrets (device codes, tokens) in logs and artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Conflicts are deterministic and explainable.
- Audit records include reservation metadata (owner, reason, expires_at).

title: Spec multi-service browser auth + profile strategy (Anthropic+Google)
description:
# Task: Spec multi-service browser auth + profile strategy (Anthropic + Google)

## Goal
Define a **robust, repeatable, secret-safe** browser automation contract that works for:
- Anthropic / Claude Code (`/login` path)
- Google / Gemini CLI (`/auth` path)

This is the “glue spec” between:
- the workflow engine (which decides *when* to authenticate)
- the account selector (which decides *which* identity to use)
- Playwright (which performs the browser steps)

## Why this matters
Browser auth is the highest-risk surface in the project:
- flows change frequently
- MFA/SSO create branching paths
- we must never leak credentials into logs/DB
- we must not “half authenticate” and then keep sending to a pane blindly

A clear spec up-front prevents brittle one-off implementations.

## Non-goals (v0.1)
- Storing passwords or OTP secrets
- Auto-solving MFA
- Headless-by-default auth

## Proposed contract
### Inputs
- `service`: `anthropic` | `google`
- `account_key`: stable identifier (matches `accounts` table primary key)
- Optional workflow-provided context:
  - `auth_url` (if CLI prints one)
  - `device_code` / `user_code` (if flow uses it)

### Outputs
- `AuthResult::Success { persisted_profile: bool }`
- `AuthResult::NeedsHuman { reason, next_steps, opened_url? }`
- `AuthResult::Failed { reason, retriable: bool }`

### Side effects
- Persisted Playwright storage state/profile per `(service, account_key)`.
- NEVER store secrets in the wa DB (DB stores only:
  - profile path
  - timestamps
  - last_success_at
  - last_failure_reason (redacted)
).

## Profile strategy
- Canonical profile directory: `~/<data_dir>/wa/browser_profiles/<service>/<account_key>/`
- We treat profiles as **opaque**: wa only creates/loads them.
- If a profile exists, attempt “already logged in” fast path.

## Reliability requirements
- Timeouts: every page wait has a hard timeout; surface actionable error.
- Deterministic logging: log only high-level milestones; redact URLs that contain tokens.
- Idempotence: if already authenticated, return success without mutating state.
- Safe failure: failures must propagate to workflow engine so it can pause and emit a user-facing action plan.

## Deliverables
- Written spec reflected as Rust types (enum + structs) and docstrings.
- A short list of selectors we will treat as "auth complete" for each service.
- A short list of selectors that indicate "MFA/password required".

## Testing
- Unit tests (offline):
  - redaction for URLs/codes
  - contract serialization stability (if we expose structured results)
- Integration tests (offline):
  - Playwright against local HTML fixtures that simulate key states (already-authenticated, needs-human)
- Manual smoke tests:
  - documented steps for validating on a real machine without embedding secrets

## Acceptance Criteria
- A reviewer can implement Anthropic + Google flows strictly from this issue without needing to consult `PLAN.md`.
- The spec explicitly names the data wa is allowed to persist and the data it must never persist.
close_reason: Added multi-service browser auth spec doc (Anthropic+Google)

title: Implement Playwright auth flow for Anthropic (Claude Code /login)
description:
# Task: Implement Playwright auth flow for Anthropic (Claude Code `/login`)

## Goal
Provide an Anthropic login helper that can bring an account into an authenticated state using Playwright + persistent profiles.

Proposed API shape (adjust only if the browser spec bead requires it):
- `async fn complete_anthropic_auth(account: &AccountRecord, ctx: &mut BrowserAutomationContext) -> AuthOutcome`

Where `AuthOutcome` is one of:
- `Success`
- `NeedsHuman { redacted_url, instructions }`
- `Failed { reason, diagnostics }`

## Expected workflow integration
`handle_usage_limits` and `handle_auth_required` for `AgentType::ClaudeCode` will:
1. send `/login` to the pane
2. parse any printed URL/code if present
3. call this browser step
4. wait for pane to become idle / ready

## Implementation outline
### Happy path (already authenticated)
- Create/load persistent profile for `(service=anthropic, account_key)`.
- Navigate to a stable landing page (likely `https://claude.ai/` or console).
- Detect an "already logged in" selector; if present, return `Success`.

### Login path (no session)
- Navigate to the correct login page (start with `https://claude.ai/login` unless `/login` prints a more specific URL).
- If prompted for email, fill using account metadata.
- Continue until either:
  - we reach the authenticated state, OR
  - we detect password/MFA/SSO interstitial

### Password/MFA/SSO handling
- **Do not** ask for, store, or type passwords.
- If a password/MFA step appears, return `NeedsHuman` with:
  - page URL to complete manually (redacted)
  - explicit next-step instructions
  - reminder that after completion, the profile will persist and future runs can be automated

## Safety requirements
- Redact any URLs containing tokens or codes in logs.
- Cap total runtime with a top-level timeout.
- Always close contexts/pages on both success and failure (no zombie browsers).

## Testing
- Integration tests (offline):
  - run Playwright against local HTML fixtures representing:
    - already-authenticated state
    - needs-human state (password/MFA)
  - validate structured outcomes and redaction

- Manual smoke tests:
  - validate on a real machine with a pre-authenticated profile

## Deliverables
- Working Anthropic auth flow using Playwright persistent profiles.
- Clear `NeedsHuman` messaging that can be surfaced by `wa robot workflow ...`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On a machine with a pre-authenticated profile, the flow returns `Success` without manual steps.
- On a machine without a profile, the flow either authenticates fully OR returns `NeedsHuman` without leaking secrets.
close_reason: done

# Task: Implement Playwright auth flow for Google (Gemini CLI `/auth`)

## Goal

## Context / why this is hard
- Google sign-in is complex (SSO, MFA, device prompts).
- Automation can be rate-limited or challenged.
- Our priority is **robustness and safety**, not full automation at any cost.

## Expected workflow integration
Gemini usage-limit workflow will:
1. send `/auth` into the Gemini CLI pane
2. parse any printed instructions (URL/code) if present
3. call this Playwright flow
4. return to the pane and resume/restart session as appropriate

- Load profile for `(service=google, account_key)`.
- Navigate to a stable page (`https://accounts.google.com/`).
- Detect a "signed-in" selector (account avatar / profile) and return `Success`.

### Login path
- If not signed in, proceed through:
  - email entry
  - account selection
  - (potentially) password/MFA — which we do NOT automate

### Password/MFA/SSO handling
- If any step requires password/MFA/SSO confirmation:
  - return `NeedsHuman` with URL and instructions (redacted)
  - keep the browser visible (non-headless) for manual completion
  - after completion, persist profile storage state

## Safety requirements
- Strict timeouts for waits.
- Redact sensitive URL parameters.
- Do not store secrets in DB.

## Testing

  - Playwright against local HTML fixtures representing:
    - already-authenticated state
    - needs-human state (password/MFA)
  - validate structured outcomes and redaction
- Manual smoke tests:

## Goal

## Design

- Non-destructive: only opens pages and checks auth state.

## Outcome taxonomy (must align with auth realities matrix)

- `Automated`
- `NeedsHuman`
- `Fail`

If the CLI chooses user-friendly labels (e.g., Success/NeedsHuman/Failed), it **must** also emit the canonical outcome field for parity.

## What to test
- Profile directory exists/created.
- Playwright initialization works.
- Service landing page reachable.

## Deliverables

- Structured error mapping so workflows can call the same code paths.

title: Cass session correlation: choose stable session key + persist external_id
description:
# Task: Cass session correlation (wa session ↔ cass session)

## Goal
Reliably correlate a wa-observed agent session (pane_id + timestamps + cwd) with a `cass` session record, and persist the linkage in wa's DB (`agent_sessions.external_id` or similar).

## Why
We need a stable way to answer:
- "Which cass transcript corresponds to this pane/session?"
- "How many tokens/messages have accumulated for this session?"

This is especially important for Claude Code where the terminal output may not provide a robust session identifier.

## Constraints
- Correlation cannot depend on fragile UI strings.
- Correlation must tolerate:
  - multiple concurrent sessions in the same repo
  - restarts/reconnects
  - slightly skewed clocks

## Proposed correlation algorithm (v0.1)
1. Determine `project_path` (from pane cwd; normalize to repo root if possible).
2. Determine `agent_type` (Claude Code).
3. Compute `start_window`: `[session_started_at - 10m, session_started_at + 10m]`.
4. `cass search --path <project_path> --agent <agent>`.
5. Filter candidates by `started_at` in window.
6. If multiple candidates remain, break ties using:
   - most recent `started_at`
   - optional: presence of unique "first prompt" hash if we can capture one
7. Persist:
   - cass session id
   - correlation confidence score + algorithm version

## Manual override
Provide a way to manually set/override correlation (config or CLI) for debugging.

## Deliverables
- `SessionCorrelation` type with: chosen id, confidence, reasons.
- Storage persistence of external_id + metadata.
- A small, deterministic test corpus for ambiguous cases.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On a fixture set with 2+ candidate cass sessions, correlation deterministically selects the intended one.
- When no candidate is found, wa records "unlinked" state without blocking other workflows.


## Testing
- Fixture corpus requirements:
  - Multiple concurrent sessions in same path (ambiguity).
  - Clock-skew variant (cass start time slightly outside window).
  - “No candidate found” variant.

- Determinism:
  - Tests must assert the chosen external_id and confidence/reasons are stable.
close_reason: Implemented cass correlation + external_meta persistence + tests

title: Token accounting via cass: aggregate tokens/messages and persist session summary
description:
# Task: Token accounting via cass

## Goal
Once a wa session is correlated to a cass session, compute and persist a compact accounting summary:
- total tokens (and/or input/output if available)
- message count
- last message timestamp

This is used for:
- status displays
- postmortems
- deciding when to rotate accounts / pause automation

## Design
- Do not store full cass transcripts in wa DB by default.
- Persist only summary fields + external session id.
- Provide an explicit "refresh" path that re-queries cass when needed.

## Implementation outline
1. Load cass session via wrapper (`cass query`).
2. Compute summary:
   - `tokens_total = sum(message.token_count)` (skip missing)
   - `messages_total = messages.len()`
   - timestamps: min(started_at), max(last message ts)
3. Persist to `agent_sessions` row for the current wa session.
4. Cache last refresh time to avoid polling cass too often.

## Deliverables
- `CassSessionSummary` type.
- Storage call(s) to upsert token accounting into `agent_sessions`.
- Strategy for refresh triggers:
  - manual (`wa status --refresh-cass`)
  - workflow step (Claude usage limit)
  - periodic background refresh (optional)

## Testing
- Covered by `wa-nu4.2.4.4` (fixtures + missing fields + missing tool behavior).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a cass JSON fixture with token_count fields, summary matches expected totals.
- Missing token_count fields do not cause failure; totals are still computed.
close_reason: Added cass session summary + refresh helper and persistence

# Phase 4 — Polish & Integration

## Objective
Make wa production-credible for daily use:
- MCP server (`fastmcp_rust`) parity with robot mode
- human-friendly CLI output (`rich_rust`)
- setup automation (SSH config parsing, remote mux bootstrap, idempotent wezterm.lua patching)
- observability & diagnostics surfaces (health JSON, metrics, diag bundles)
- external tool integrations (`cass`, `caut` deepening)

## Why this phase exists
Even correct automation fails without:
- introspection (why is it stuck?)
- diagnostics (what happened last hour?)
- fast operator workflows (setup and repair)

## Deliverables
- MCP server: tools + resources mapped to wa-core.
- `wa doctor` and `wa status --health`.
- Optional Prometheus endpoint for watchers.
- Diagnostic bundle generator (`wa diag bundle`).
- Setup commands: `wa setup` for local+remote canonical WezTerm mux infrastructure.
- Strong test suite + CI-friendly checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- A robot-mode agent can operate wa exclusively via MCP tools.
- A human can bootstrap a new remote host with `wa setup remote` and get persistent mux sessions.
- Diagnostic bundle captures enough to debug a stuck workflow without attaching a debugger.



## Success Criteria
- Human UX, MCP integration, setup automation, diagnostics, and ship-readiness are in place with high operator trust.
- E2E + CI runs are stable and produce artifacts; failures are diagnosable.
- The project is "installable and usable" by someone new via docs/quickstart.


## Testing
- Contract stability tests:
  - MCP parity vs robot outputs and schemas (see `wa-nu4.3.1.*`, `wa-nu4.3.1.5`).
  - Human CLI snapshot tests must avoid ANSI when not a TTY and be stable across terminals.

- Setup/ops E2E:
  - `wa setup` and `wa setup remote` must have idempotency E2E scripts with full artifacts (see `wa-nu4.3.3.*`).

- Diagnostics tests:
  - `wa doctor` fixtures cover healthy + broken states and produce predictable advice and artifact bundles.

- CI reliability:
  - CI must upload artifacts on failure and include enough logs to debug without rerunning.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Deliverables.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

## Cross-references
- **wa-3dfxb** (Scripting engine epic): The MCP server in this phase should follow the same tool/resource patterns established by the scripting engine. MCP integration patterns (tool registration, schema validation, capability negotiation) must be consistent between the scripting engine's extension points and the MCP server's tool surface. Coordinate to avoid divergent tool schemas.

## macOS Compatibility Requirements
- All CLI commands (`wa doctor`, `wa status`, `wa setup`) must work on macOS (the primary development platform) as well as Linux.
- Setup automation must handle macOS-specific differences: no systemd (use launchd or user-level process management), Homebrew paths for WezTerm, and macOS-native SSH agent forwarding.
- Diagnostic bundle generation must use portable commands (no `journalctl`; fall back to `log show` on macOS or log file collection).
- E2E tests that rely on Docker must account for Docker Desktop for Mac limitations (see wa-nu4.3.3.11).

description:
# [EPIC] MCP server (fastmcp_rust)

## Mission
Expose wa’s core capabilities via MCP (Model Context Protocol) so AI agents can use wa as a tool provider with:
- stable tool names
- stable JSON schemas
- low-token, machine-friendly responses
- strong safety guarantees (policy gates)

## Why MCP matters
Robot mode (`wa robot ...`) is great for shells, but MCP is the native integration surface for many agent runtimes.
A first-class MCP server makes wa more composable and enables “swarm” behaviors without brittle CLI parsing.

## Guiding principles
- **Parity with robot mode**: MCP tools call the same underlying functions as `wa robot`.
- **No new logic**: MCP is a transport / surface, not a second implementation.
- **Safe by default**: anything that sends input to panes must pass PolicyEngine.
- **Resources are read-only**: resources provide snapshots; actions are tools.

## Definition of done
- MCP server builds behind `--features mcp`.
- Tools + resources cover the Appendix A.3 surface from the plan.
- Tool outputs are deterministic and versioned.

## Notes for future-self
If parity drifts, treat it as a bug. Add tests that exercise both MCP and robot paths with the same fixtures.


## Success Criteria
- MCP tools/resources are implemented by delegating to robot/core APIs (no duplicated business logic).
- MCP responses are stable, schema-validated where applicable, and integrate with audit/policy.
- Tests cover MCP request/response parsing and tool behavior on allow/deny paths.


## Testing
- Parity tests:
  - For each MCP tool, run the equivalent robot/core call with the same fixture inputs and assert identical semantics (success shape, error codes, redaction).

- Schema/contract tests:
  - Validate MCP request/response bodies against the declared schemas.
  - Ensure stable error codes and version fields.

- Safety tests:
  - Explicit allow/deny scenarios prove PolicyEngine gates MCP actions exactly as it gates robot/human paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Definition of Done.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

title: MCP audit integration: record each tool call decision/outcome (redacted)
description:
# Task: MCP audit integration

## Goal
Ensure MCP usage is trustworthy by recording an audit record for each MCP tool call.

MCP is high-risk because it is typically invoked by an agent. We need:
- a trace of what was requested
- why it was allowed/denied
- what was actually executed

## Requirements
- For each MCP tool invocation:
  - record tool name
  - record a redacted summary of arguments
  - record policy decision and preconditions
  - record outcome (success/error) and elapsed time
- Link audit entries to any underlying action audit entries (send/workflow).

## Redaction
- Do not store secrets or full inputs.
- Store hashes/summaries consistent with the shared redaction system.

## Testing
- MCP tests (`wa-nu4.3.1.5`) must cover:
  - tool call emits an audit record on allow AND deny
  - redaction behavior on representative arg payloads
  - linkage between MCP audit record and underlying action audit record (when applicable)
  - reservation tool calls (`wa.reserve`/`wa.release`) emit audit rows

## Acceptance Criteria
- Calling an MCP tool always results in an audit entry, even when denied.
- Audit entries are sufficient to debug a failed MCP automation without reproducing.


LABELS: area-audit, area-mcp, phase-4

DEPENDS ON

# [EPIC] Human CLI UX (rich_rust)

## Mission
Make wa pleasant and fast to use for humans while staying scriptable.

## Philosophy
- Default output is **human-friendly** when attached to a TTY.
- When piped (non-TTY), output becomes machine-friendly and stable.
- The same underlying data models feed:
  - `wa status/events/query/...` (human)
  - `wa robot ...` (machine)
  - MCP (machine)

## What this epic covers
- Rendering with `rich_rust` (tables, panels, highlighting)
- Command ergonomics (flags, defaults, exit codes)
- Clear error messages and remediation hints

## Testing & stability (non-negotiable)
This epic is “done” only if humans can trust the output contracts.

- Snapshot tests:
  - stable table/panel rendering in a non-ANSI test mode
  - stable ordering and truncation rules

- Contract tests:
  - each human command has deterministic exit codes
  - when non-TTY / `--format json`, output is machine-parseable and schema-stable

- E2E coverage:
  - the E2E harness must exercise the human surfaces for the most common workflows:
    - status/events triage
    - policy-gated send
    - running a workflow manually
    - accounts/rules diagnosis

(Concrete test beads in this epic: `wa-nu4.3.2.10` and `wa-nu4.3.2.11`.)

## Success Criteria
- A human can diagnose and fix a stuck agent using:
  - `wa status`
  - `wa events --unhandled`
  - `wa workflow handle_usage_limits <pane>`
  - `wa doctor`
without reading source.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All scope described in this bead is implemented without omission.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

# Task: Output layer (rich_rust + TTY auto-detect)

## Goal

- Event panel/list (events)

  - rich output normalized (strip timestamps/ANSI as needed)
  - plain output has zero ANSI escape sequences
  - json output validates against a documented schema/envelope
